verdict.rationale: Jev's core API returns typed answers via three question primitives (Choice, Score, Noul) each with well-defined structured fields (option/probability/confidence, score/probability distribution/confidence, yes-probability), and SDKs (Python/JS) expose typed clients and typed responses so developers avoid fragile string parsing; JSON structure is also accepted for instructions/options/criteria. Community testimony confirms real usage building classifiers/decisions off these typed outputs. missing for 10: no explicit JSON-schema-constrained free-form output mode (only fixed primitive types), no independent benchmark of parsing reliability, and one community complaint about confidence calibration being 'fake' introduces a minor quality caveat.
